ground.note: The page and the navigation rail. Night is the dome.

paper.note: Panels, bars, cards, inputs, ring bodies.

hairline.note: Every 1px border, divider and grid gap.

hairline-strong.note: Inputs, chips, switch track, scrollbar thumb, dot grid.

ink.note: 17:1 on paper by day. Night ink is bone.

ink-faint.note: 4.9:1 on paper, 4.6:1 on ground by day.

brass.note: Instrument marks only: tracks, ticks, rules, selection marks. Never a button, never running text.

brass-faint.note: Idle ring track, rule tracks, table head rule.

beam.note: The one action colour. White text 5.8:1 by day.

beam-subtle.note: Picked option, your bubble, the next code tile.

ai.note: Only for AI-made or AI-making things, always labelled.

body-1.note: Shared-character ring and avatar fill, slot 1.

night-ground.note: Night ground; also pinned on the site's first and last bands, the presenter and audience views, and the dialog backdrop at 50%.

narrative.overview:
circloo is an orrery of people. A circle is a ring, its members are bodies on that ring, and a round is a transit everyone watches together. The world is built from the orrery's materials and nothing else: two grounds (a cool off-white by Day, the dome #070e1a by Night), ink for everything that is read, brass for every mark that measures something, one beam of blue for the one thing to do, violet only where AI wrote something, and the five mood skies as fills. It refuses the SaaS dashboard (white cards on grey, one accent) and the enterprise sidebar-as-identity it replaced (issue #250).

The chrome is quiet so three things can carry colour: the people (characters and avatars keep their fixed colours in both themes), the face (the "oo" of the wordmark, coral mouth), and the content (an icebreaker set large on a dealt card, a live canvas, a reveal). Density is medium: 15px body on a 4px grid, panels with one hairline, lists that stagger in. Rings, arcs, ticks and hairlines are the only ornament, and each one carries data: who is on the ring, how far the round has run, which option is picked, where the time stands.

Night is a full theme, not an inversion. Some surfaces are pinned to the dome in both themes because a room reads best with light content on a dark ground: the public site's first and last bands, the presenter view and the audience screen. Those surfaces redeclare the Night tokens as literals so every shared component inside follows.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, Day and Night, with every text pair AA or better in both.
The ring is the signature: brass track, bodies at equal angles, the circle's sky inside, a brass arc while a round runs, mirrored in RTL.
Brass measures, beam acts, violet means AI, coral is the mouth. Nothing else is coloured.
One family (Readex Pro, variable) for Latin and Arabic; hierarchy by scale and weight; the instrument numeral's weight follows the mood.
Hairline grids: cells share one hairline, cards do not float in a grid.
One motion grammar (duration tokens, three springs, exponential ease-out), every animation with a reduced-motion path that keeps the meaning.
Four languages, logical properties, Arabic as a first-class mirrored layout.

rules.name: The Violet Rule
rules.body: If it is violet, AI made it. If AI made it, it is labelled.

rules.name: The Brass Measures Rule
rules.body: Every brass mark carries data (a track, a progress, a tick, a selection, a rule under a running time). Brass is never a button, never running text, never decoration.

rules.name: The One Beam Rule
rules.body: One primary button per view. Beam is spent on the next action and on nothing else.

rules.name: The Coral Rule
rules.body: Coral is the mouth. No badge, no dot, no accent anywhere else.

rules.name: The Sky With a Word Rule
rules.body: A sky fill never stands alone: the mood's icon and word sit beside it, so colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Night is a full theme defined once in tokens.css under [data-theme='dark'] and under prefers-color-scheme: dark when the person chose "Match my device". A surface that must stay on the dome in both themes (the site's first and last bands, the presenter and audience views) redeclares the Night values as literals with the legacy aliases, so every shared component inside follows without a second stylesheet.

rules.name: The Weight Axis Rule
rules.body: Only the reading numeral drives Readex Pro's weight axis, and only the circle's mood drives it. Everywhere else, weights are 400 (body), 500 (controls, chips), 600 (headings, names), 700 (wordmark and lozenges).

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: No second typeface, no monospace. Codes and times are Readex Pro with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px hairline before it is a shadow. A shadow means the thing floats above the page (a menu, a card dealt from the deck, a sheet); content at rest gets raised at most.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: No glows, no blurred colour halos, no glass. The only "ring" around a control is a focus ring (2px focus, 2px offset) or a brass selection ring.

dos: Do keep the chrome to ground, paper, ink and brass, and let people, the face and the content carry colour.
Do spend beam on exactly one primary action per view; selection is beam-subtle (nav, options) or a brass tick (segmented controls).
Do keep violet for AI alone and label every AI output (lozenge, name or "Suggested by AI").
Do put every sky fill beside the mood's icon and word; mood is never colour alone.
Do separate with a 1px hairline first; shadows are for things that float (menus, dealt cards, sheets).
Do set every count, time and code in tabular numerals; drive only the reading numeral's weight, and only by mood.
Do use logical properties and --dir style custom properties so rings, drawers and switches mirror in RTL; drop uppercase and tracking under :lang(ar).
Do give every entrance a reduced-motion path that keeps the meaning (a fade, an instant position, a pop by opacity).
Do use Lucide icons at 14–20px, stroke 2, with .flip-rtl on directional ones.
donts: Don't add a second typeface, a monospace, or a system display face; Readex Pro at every size.
Don't paint gradients, glass (backdrop-filter), glows or blurred halos. The 24px dot grid of the whiteboard and the dome bands is the one radial-gradient, and it draws dots.
Don't use coral outside the face's mouth, brass as a button or running text, or violet as decoration.
Don't float cards in a grid; neighbours share a hairline (1px gap on a hairline background).
Don't use emoji as icons or sparkles for AI; the bird's moods and the violet label are the AI signal.
Don't hide a control's label with display: none; clip it (.visually-hidden or the .btn__label clip).
Don't run a loop that is not a live indicator (typing dots, the thinking crest, a conversion spinner, the presence pulse); a count pops once, a status dot pulses once.
Don't nest panels or put a panel head inside a hairline-grid cell.
